newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up, investors seen value-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up, investors seen value-hunting.

text.p: Russian shares rose in healthy volumes on Thursday but traders said leading shares would be stable on Friday as some investors switched their attention to less liquid undervalued stocks.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose to 357.00 after 349.75 on Wednesday. Total market volume was a vigorous $51.7 million and many shares were at near-record levels.
"I expect there will be sideways movements and perhaps weakness during the day but overall stable (tomorrow)," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze.
National power utility UES rose to $0.3056 from $0.2999 on Wednesday but off an early high of $0.3100. Regional power company Mosenergo eased to $1.348 from $1.350.
Norilsk Nickel metals group rose about six percent to $6.35 from $5.97 on Wednesday.

CSFB chief trader Igor Rozhkov said money which started coming in over the last two weeks was still making itself felt, although others said investors were transferring their interest to less liquid stocks which trade on the RTS-2.
The RTS-2 is for less well known shares and sees far lower volumes than the main RTS.
Operators said "energos", or regional power utilities, and heavy construction were doing best.
"They are the definite outperformers of the market -- the price action there is just wild," said a trader with a Western bank. "People are looking for value, looking for laggers."

Gazprom ADRs shot up two marks on the Berlin Stock Exchange to marks 29.20 at GMT 1530 from Wednesday's closing 27.10 after Gazprom said it would protect its plan for separate foreign and domestic share markets.
Underlying Gazprom shares closed almost unchanged at $0.6439 after $0.6415.
One trader said the Russian market could be in for a jolt next week if the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to raise interest rates at its May 20 meeting.
"If they do come out of the blue and raise rates the market will be hit hard," said the trader at a Western bank. "The market is overly bullish and it will hit us hard."
